text: the Bible is not a univocal text the notion that it is is a Dogma that one just chooses to accept because of the
implications hey everybody I'm Dan mlen I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion to say the Bible is univocal is to say
that every last word speaks from a single unified and consistent perspective and with a single unified
and consistent voice in other words it cannot disagree with itself it cannot contradict itself self and there are
absolutely no data that support that conclusion the Bible is made up of numerous different texts written by
authors in different time periods in different languages to different audiences for different reasons and from very different perspectives and when we
try to impose this unifying framework of univocality we are silencing the authors
themselves because it means more to us to have the Bible be consistent than the
actual messages of the authors and so we have to create a new and a different third thing in order to create Harmony
in order to reconcile those voices and neither those voices themselves nor the unifying framework that we impose upon
them transcends our social our historical our rhetorical contexts we are all speaking from within those
contexts engaging with those contexts which is why those unifying Frameworks are always changing there are no data
that support the univocality of the Bible we impose a unifying framework on the Bible if we have decided we want it
to be univocal and we are just reflecting our own needs and circumstances and how we create more
meaning and significance with the biblical text and far too often that involves structuring power and values
and boundaries and does not involve trying to make us better people
